registryStatement.content:
1. Data Controller

DATA_CONTROLLER

2. Contact Person for the Registry

DATA_CONTACT_PERSON, {adminEmailLink}.

3. Name of the Registry

{appName} - Candidate Information System.

4. Legal Basis and Purpose of Processing Personal Data

The legal basis for processing personal data under the EU General Data Protection Regulation is the individual's consent. The purpose of processing personal data is its use in the election compass.

5. Content of the Registry

The registry stores the following data: name, political background, email address, date of birth, website URLs, social media profile URLs, other voluntary responses to the election compass's questions, and information obtained from public electoral registers.

DATA_STORAGE_TERM_EG_5_YRS

Cookies necessary for the functionality of the service are processed based on legitimate interest, for example, to ensure security.

6. Regular Sources of Information

Data stored in the registry is obtained from candidates through an online form, during their bank authentication, and from public electoral registers.

7. Regular Disclosures of Data and Transfers Outside the EU or EEA

Data is not regularly disclosed to other parties, but after the publication of the election compass ends, the data may be used for research purposes and to develop the election compass.

8. Principles of Registry Protection

The processing of the registry is carried out with care, and data processed through information systems is adequately protected. When registry data is stored on Internet servers, appropriate measures are taken to ensure both physical and digital security. The data controller ensures that stored data, server access rights, and other critical personal data security information are handled confidentially and only by employees whose job description includes such responsibilities.

9. Right of Access and Right to Request Data Correction

Every individual in the registry has the right to check their stored data and request correction of any incorrect or incomplete data. If a person wishes to check their stored data or request corrections, they must send a request via email to the data controller. The data controller may request the individual to verify their identity if necessary. The data controller responds within the timeframe set by the EU General Data Protection Regulation.

10. Other Rights Related to Personal Data Processing

Individuals in the registry have the right to request the deletion of their personal data from the registry (’right to be forgotten’). Similarly, registered individuals have other rights under the EU General Data Protection Regulation, such as the right to restrict the processing of personal data in certain situations. Requests must be sent via email to the data controller. The data controller may request the individual to verify their identity if necessary. The data controller responds within the timeframe set by the EU General Data Protection Regulation.

info.content:
About Democracy

Sweden is a democracy. This means that the people help decide how the country is governed. As voters, we elect the politicians we believe are best suited to lead society. These politicians then make political decisions. We elect politicians to the Parliament (Riksdag), the regions, and the municipalities.

Four Elections in Sweden

General elections are held every four years. The next election will take place on Sunday, 13 September 2026, when elections will be held for the Parliament (Riksdag), regional councils, and municipal councils.

The parliamentary election determines which political parties will govern Sweden. The regional elections choose the politicians who govern each region and make decisions about healthcare and regional public transport. The municipal elections choose the politicians who govern each municipality and make decisions about schools, preschools (daycare), and elderly care.

Every five years, Sweden also holds elections to the European Parliament.

Who Can Vote?

To vote in any election, you must be at least 18 years old. To vote in the Parliamentary election and the European Parliament election, you must be a Swedish citizen. To vote in regional or municipal elections, you must have lived in Sweden for three years or more, but you do not need to be a Swedish citizen.

How Can I Vote?

Before the election, the Swedish Election Authority sends a voting card to everyone who is eligible to vote. Your voting card shows:

  • your name,
  • which elections you are entitled to vote in, and
  • the polling station where you should vote.

When and Where Can I Vote?

  • On Election Day (13 September): vote at the polling station listed on your voting card.
  • Advance voting: you may vote in advance anywhere in Sweden from 26 August 2026 through 12 September 2026.

How to Vote at a Polling Station

Bring your ID card or other valid identification to the polling station. The address and opening hours of your polling station are printed on your voting card.

When you vote, you use three ballot papers and three envelopes. The ballot papers are colour-coded:

  • Yellow – Parliamentary election (Riksdag)
  • Blue – Regional election
  • White – Municipal election

Choose one party for each election and place the corresponding ballot paper in the correct envelope. You may vote for different political parties in the three different elections if you wish.

Some ballot papers also list the names of candidates. If you wish, you can cast a personal vote by marking the box next to the name of the candidate you want to support. You may mark only one candidate on each ballot paper.

Choose your ballot papers in private. Prepare your vote behind a voting screen. Place one ballot paper in one envelope for each election. Hand the envelopes to the election officials. Your vote is always secret.

More Information

For more information about elections and voting in Sweden, visit the website of the Swedish Election Authority: https://www.val.se

If you would like to learn more about the political parties and their policies, visit their official websites:

  • Centerpartiet
  • Kristdemokraterna
  • Liberalerna
  • Miljöpartiet
  • Moderaterna
  • Socialdemokraterna
  • Sverigedemokraterna
  • Vänsterpartiet
